title: Before Induction Safety Check
summary: Run the Sign In phase and the equipment check before anesthesia, and stop the case when a safety check fails.
scenario: The patient is in the operating room and awake. Before induction, the team performs the Sign In phase of the surgical safety checklist and the anesthesia machine and equipment check. You are the anesthesia nurse responsible for making sure nothing is skipped.
objectives: Place the Sign In phase in the surgical safety checklist
Recall the order of Sign In items
Detect unsafe entries on the checklist
Verify machine and equipment, and respond to a failed check

patient.procedure: Elective left knee arthroscopy under general anesthesia

history: No chronic illness, no regular medication
Reports itchy skin after wearing latex gloves

steps.title: Which phase?
steps.situation: The patient is in the operating room, awake, and induction has not started.
steps.prompt: Which phase of the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist applies now?

options.text: Sign Out (before the patient leaves the operating room)

steps.explanation: The Sign In phase takes place before induction of anesthesia. Time Out is before incision and Sign Out is before the patient leaves the room.
steps.takeaway: Sign In = before induction. Time Out = before incision. Sign Out = before leaving.

steps.title: Sign In order
steps.prompt: Arrange the Sign In items in the order they appear on the WHO checklist.

items.text: Confirm identity, site, procedure and consent
Confirm the surgical site is marked
Confirm the anesthesia safety check is complete
Confirm the pulse oximeter is on the patient and working
Assess difficult airway or aspiration risk

steps.explanation: The WHO Sign In section starts with identity, site, procedure and consent, then site marking, the anesthesia safety check, pulse oximeter, allergy, and difficult airway or aspiration risk.
steps.takeaway: Learn the checklist order so no item is skipped under pressure.

steps.title: Spot the unsafe entries
steps.instruction: Select every entry that is incorrect or unsafe.
steps.prompt: The team has ticked the following Sign In items. Which entries must be corrected before induction?

items.label: Patient confirmed identity, site, procedure and consent
Site marking: left knee not marked ('will mark after induction')
items.why: The site must be marked while the patient is awake and can confirm it.

items.label: Pulse oximeter on the patient and functioning
Allergy: 'No known allergy' ticked, although the patient reported itching with latex gloves
items.why: A reported latex reaction contradicts the ticked entry and must be clarified and communicated.

items.label: Anesthesia safety check (machine and medication) completed
Difficult airway and aspiration risk assessed, equipment available

steps.explanation: Two entries are unsafe: the site was not marked while the patient was awake, and the allergy entry contradicts the history. Both must be fixed before induction.
steps.takeaway: A ticked box is only safe when it matches the facts.

steps.title: Machine and equipment check
steps.instruction: Select the items that must be verified before induction.
steps.prompt: Which items belong to the anesthesia machine and equipment check?

items.label: Oxygen supply connected and backup oxygen cylinder available
items.why: Loss of oxygen supply must be covered by a backup.

items.label: Monitor alarms audible and limits appropriate
items.why: Alarms only help when they are on and set correctly.

items.label: Gas scavenging system connected
items.why: Protects staff from waste anesthetic gas.

items.label: Surgical instrument count sheet
items.why: A surgical team task, not part of the machine check.

items.label: Post-operative bed assignment
items.why: Not part of the machine check.

steps.explanation: The pre-use check covers oxygen supply and backup, leak test, backup ventilation, suction, monitor alarms and scavenging. Surgical instrument counts, bed assignment and sutures belong to other checks.
steps.takeaway: Check what keeps the patient oxygenated, ventilated and monitored.

steps.title: Failed leak test
steps.situation: During the circuit leak test the pressure will not hold. You suspect a loose connection but have not found it. The team is waiting.

options.text: Do not proceed to induction. Recheck connections or replace the circuit or machine, repeat the check and inform the anesthesiologist
options.consequence: Induction is delayed until the equipment is confirmed safe, and the anesthesiologist is informed.

options.text: Proceed, because a small leak can be compensated with higher fresh gas flow
options.consequence: Starting with a known leak risks inadequate ventilation and delivery of gas to the patient.

options.text: Recheck all connections and retest, but tell nobody until it is fixed
options.consequence: Rechecking is right, but the anesthesiologist must be told that the check failed.

options.text: Skip the leak test, because the machine passed its checks yesterday
options.consequence: The pre-use check must be done before each case.

steps.explanation: A failed pre-use check means the machine is not ready. Fix or replace the equipment, repeat the check and inform the anesthesiologist before induction.
steps.takeaway: A failed check stops the case until it passes.

steps.title: Follow-up: replacement circuit
steps.situation: A replacement breathing circuit has been fitted.
steps.prompt: What must happen before the machine is used?

options.text: Repeat the leak test and relevant checks on the new set-up, and confirm the result to the anesthesiologist
Nothing: a new circuit is always safe
Only check that the circuit looks intact
Test it after induction has begun

steps.explanation: Any change to the breathing system requires the checks to be repeated. Visual inspection alone cannot detect a leak.
steps.takeaway: Change the equipment, repeat the check.

steps.title: Medication labelling
steps.situation: Syringes of anesthetic medication have been drawn up by the team and are on the tray.
steps.prompt: What must be true before any medication is given?

options.text: Every syringe is clearly labelled (drug name, concentration) and verified before administration
Unlabelled syringes are acceptable if used immediately
Only the first syringe needs a label
Labels can be added after the case

steps.explanation: Unlabelled syringes are a major source of medication errors. Each syringe must be labelled and verified before it is given.
